newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concerned about more violence in Burma.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concerned about more violence in Burma.

text.p: The United States expressed grave concern on Friday about possible further violence in Burma this weekend and said it would hold the military junta responsible for any attack on its democratic opponents.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Burma's military leaders were reportedly organising more demonstrations by the Union Solidarity Development Association, which he described as "a front organisation for the military dictators" and the group responsible for the attack on Nov. 9 on democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi's motorcade.

"The United States is gravely concerned by reports about the potential for violence this weekend in Rangoon in the wake of an extremely disturbing attack last weekend by hired thugs on Aung San Suu Kyi," Burns said in a statement to reporters.
"And we understand that this demonstration may be held with the express purpose of provoking further violence in Rangoon," he added.
Burns said Washington had "clear evidence" that the attack on the motorcade was organised by the Union Solidarity group.
He said Washington rejected attempts by the military junta, the State Law And Order Restoration Council (SLORC), to blame this attack on the democracy activists.

"We and the international community will hold the SLORC responsible for any violent attack, or any harm that may come to Aung Sun Suu Kyi, other senior leaders of the National League for Democracy, or other supporters of the democratic opposition," Burns said.
Aung Sun Suu Kyi and her fellow democrats have demonstrated repeatedly their strong commitment to non-violent expression of their political views.

Washington called on the SLORC to punish those responsible for the Nov. 9 attack, prevent further violent incidents and engage in discussions with pro-democracy groups about the country's political future.
